chosen.title: Robots Go Public: What the Humanoid Robotics IPO Wave Actually Means
chosen.rationale: Agility Robotics just announced a SPAC merger valuing it at ~$2.5B and raising $620M+ — the largest capital raise in humanoid robotics history and the category's first pure-play public listing — while Hyundai's Atlas performed at the World Cup and UBTECH logged 13,000+ Chinese orders in the same week. This is the moment humanoid robotics stops being a demo and becomes an investable industry, exactly the mechanism-plus-frontier story Kenji's maker/engineer readers want explained.

rejected_candidates.title: Data Centers Leave the Ground: Inside the Race to Compute in Orbit
rejected_candidates.rationale: AI's power appetite is colliding with terrestrial grid limits, and SpaceX and others are now racing to put data centers in orbit to tap solar power directly and sidestep cooling/land constraints — a genuinely new collision of Kenji's aerospace and AI beats, and a mechanism story (orbital thermal management, latency, launch economics) no one else on staff would reach for.

sources.name: Forbes — 7 Space Science and Technology Breakthroughs 2026

rejected_candidates.title: Teaching Robots to Dream: How World Models Are Making Physical AI Actually Work
rejected_candidates.rationale: NVIDIA's newly released Isaac GR00T and Cosmos world models are the actual mechanism behind 2026's headline shift of 'physical AI' from proof-of-concept to deployed systems — robots learning from simulated, synthetic experience rather than costly real-world trial and error. It's a frontier-and-mechanism piece tailor-made for Kenji's 'how does this actually work' sequence, distinct from prior AIMA coverage of humanoid factory-floor tasks.
